specimen.revision: Photo marking matches the board family/revision in kbdbabel; component substitutions and electrical identity still require verification.
specimen.rom: User confirms the museum keyboard has a replacement keyboard ROM (2026-10-17). Contents unread; original ROM may be located later. S600 remains reference firmware. A replaceable ROM or differing label is not evidence of a PCB revision.

gaps.detail: Zander placement download remains unusable, but manufacturer PDF page 10, drawing 63-330-4103-2, provides populated reference placement. It supports reviewed DIP/discrete identities and BR location candidates; it does not establish specimen terminal continuity or solder-side copper.

Assigned native copper and its observation/inference status are recorded in route-evidence.json and generated/layout.json. The physical data/clock path, A1 terminal correspondence, CPU endpoint and specimen WR/RD disagreement remain unresolved. Unassigned artwork is not electrical connectivity. The CPU CLK candidate remains withdrawn: comparison photos weaken the earlier apparent D6 conflict but do not establish primary-specimen cross-side correspondence. See routeReviews for the conflicting and superseding observations.

Board envelope and placement scale remain nominal rather than measured. Top-photo landmarks and local underside fits support bounded geometry review; sockets and raised leads obscure some board entries. Global underside registration remains unqualified. generated/photo-registration.json and generated/bottom-registration.json retain current residuals, independent checks and extrapolation limits. A local fit does not authorize a global artwork warp or copper assignment.
RC oscillator and propagation delays are not measured.

Current native placements and unplaced references are authoritative in generated/layout.json; component-evidence.json records their pin-assignment basis. R4.2/R7/R8 are placed using the reviewed common underside strip and reference ground assignment. Transistor body axes are visual observations only, with electrical lead mapping unresolved. R6.4/R6.5 candidates identify visible lead ends rather than qualified holes. Remaining discrete and connector terminal maps require further evidence; C5.5 lead entry is obscured by the adjacent electrolytic.

Zander connects WR to the output inverter; kbdbabel connects RD and leaves WR unused. Resolve by following specimen copper/continuity. The current HDL explicitly models the Zander reference. Robotron service handbook pp. 89–90 explicitly supports WR. Specimen continuity remains unverified.

serviceInterfaces.scope: Zander reference topology. Factory placement drawing supports BR1/BR2 photo location candidates; their terminal order, continuity and construction remain unverified. Terminal numbers are reconstruction identifiers, not observed pad markings.

bridges.role: Isolates the oscillator output from the CPU clock input.
bridges.testUse: Opening the bridge permits external clock injection on the CPU side; inferred electrical use, not a documented factory procedure.

physicalEvidence.location: Beyond A7 near the ROM end, beside C6/R10.3
physicalEvidence.observation: The original-top-photo left BR1 terminal and R10.3 left lead correspond to a locally connected underside joint pair. Their common reference net is CLK: left BR1 is pin 2 (CPU side), right is pin 1 (oscillator side). This is photo-supported reference orientation, not measured continuity or proof of the complete CPU/oscillator paths.

terminalMapping.2: left original-photo endpoint; reference CLK, local R10.3 link

bridges.role: Isolates the reset circuit output from the CPU active-low RESET input.
bridges.testUse: Opening the bridge permits controlled reset injection on the CPU side; inferred electrical use, not a documented factory procedure.

physicalEvidence.location: Cable side of A1, beside R9.1
physicalEvidence.observation: A wire-like link is visible between two solder terminals at the factory-designated bridge location. Electrical continuity, construction and source/CPU terminal order are unverified. Endpoint array order is photographic, not schematic pin numbering.

referenceTiming.scope: Documented reference values, not measurements of this specimen. Existing 683 kHz emulator clock lies within this reference range.

referenceVariants.scope: Factory schematic gate pin assignments agree with the current electrical reference. Factory placement identifies the three photo locations; corrected PCB placements and photo landmarks retain stable schematic/HDL refs. This is a reconstruction correction, not evidence of a board variant.
referenceVariants.note: A2 placements corrected after reviewing all 12 NAND gates. A6/A7 printed package labels remain a separate type comparison; chip models unchanged.

referenceVariants.scope: Third branch goes to V4.8 base in both drawings. This is a source numbering disagreement, not proven board revision or circuit-topology difference. Native reference connectivity remains the Zander transcription. Neither drawing supplies a complete ten-lead package map.

sourceReviews.method: Reviewed contents on PDF page 2, keyboard sheets and a contact sheet of all 50 PDF pages.
sourceReviews.finding: No keyboard solder-side copper drawing identified in this 50-page source. The contents list keyboard layout, populated placement and schematic. This is a scoped search result, not proof that no copper drawing exists elsewhere.
sourceReviews.remainingUse: Placement identities and schematic connectivity can be reviewed against these sheets; precise specimen routing still needs photo or continuity evidence.

sourceReviews.method: Read the face after rotating the comparison photograph 180 degrees; compare its board-edge and transistor-row context with factory placement PDF page 10 and the primary top photograph.
sourceReviews.finding: The upright white bank corresponds to R1, not A1. The visible face reads 3894 and V D beside a logo; the meaning of those markings is unresolved.

identityBasis.detail: R1 lies between the sensing-transistor row and the long board edge; R2 lies on the other side of the sensing-transistor region. This identifies bodies, not numbered terminals.

sourceReviews.remainingUse: Package appearance and lead construction. Reference terminal order, common terminal, resistance and primary board entries require separate evidence.

sourceReviews.finding: Primary R1 and R2 each expose ten raised lead exits. Comparison R1 oblique independently shows ten. The native nine-terminal reference symbols cannot be used directly as complete physical package maps. Factory R2 third branch is labelled 10 versus 8 in Zander.
sourceReviews.scope: Lead observations and drawing labels only; no inferred common duplication, unused terminal, installed numbering or net reassignment. Photo pixels and interpretation limits are in component-evidence.json terminalReview.

sourceReviews.finding: KWH 3894 is eight 910-ohm resistors with common terminal 1, branches 2 through 9 and unused terminal 10. This identifies the comparison R1 marking and explains its ten visible leads without an extra resistor. B1 nominal pitch is 2.5 mm, not 2.54 mm.
sourceReviews.scope: Package-reference identification only. Primary R1 and installed pin-one orientation require separate evidence. The catalog 3845 is nine 4.7-kOhm resistors and remains only a candidate for R2; no unseen marking inferred.

routeReviews.summary: CPU-side clock trace assignment withdrawn: the projected round terminal appears to connect to A4:13 D6 on the top photo, conflicting with the tentative CLK origin at A5:6. Local geometric fit checks do not prove a solder joint or through-board connection. No CLK or D6 route is assigned from this observation. New separate-specimen photos show an apparent CPU pin-6 trace and a likely matching top terminal whose narrow trace passes between A4 leads 12 and 13; this weakens the apparent D6 conflict, but terminal correspondence remains provisional.

bottomObservation.origin: Tentative apparent junction at A5:6; electrical attachment unresolved

topTerminalCandidate.apparentConnection: A4:13 /D6; cross-side terminal identity not proven

routeReviews.nextEvidence: Use the recorded comparison CPU pin count and terminal pixels to check both-side correspondence and the primary image before restoring any route. Hidden continuation, primary-specimen end-to-end clock continuity and measurements remain open.

bottom.cpuPinNumbering: Component-side CPU notch faces the middle of the board. Viewed from the underside, count inward-row pin 1 at the middle-facing end toward pin 20 at the ROM end; reverse the top-view handedness. All 20 joints are visible in this image.
bottom.observation: A visible underside trace runs from the sixth CPU joint to the round terminal between the CPU and A4. This is a comparison-specimen observation, not primary-specimen geometry.

top.observation: The likely matching terminal has a narrow trace running between A4 leads 12 and 13 toward the package underside. A distinct neighbouring trace comes from lead 13. The package obscures the continuation. Terminal correspondence remains provisional; no through-board or hidden connection is asserted.

comparisonReview.conclusion: The sharper comparison photos weaken the prior apparent D6-conflict interpretation. They do not justify substituting a D6 route or restoring the primary CLK route without checking terminal correspondence and the primary image. Preserve the withdrawn geometry until that review is complete.

correspondenceFit.method: tools/photo_registration.py homography and project; four CPU corner anchors, independent intermediate pin checks. Coordinates are original image pixels.
correspondenceFit.limitations: CPU top lead feet and the package obscure true hole centres. The terminal is outside the CPU corner hull, so this is extrapolation. The fit supports further review of the candidate but does not establish a through-board connection or primary-specimen geometry. No physical dimensional tolerance is claimed.

routeReviews.summary: BR2 remains unplaced. Separate-specimen close-ups show the bridge wire and a trace leaving the ROM-facing endpoint toward the long board-edge corridor. The two underside endpoint candidates are identifiable by their relation to the R9 resistor bank, but no complete path to CPU RESET or V4.9 collector has been established. CPU pin 26 has no visible underside trace at its solder joint in the reviewed close-up; this is not evidence of a disconnected pin.

endpointObservations.endpointOrder: ROM-facing, cable-facing; geometric names only, not electrical source/CPU sides
ROM-facing, cable-facing; provisional local correspondence from adjacent R9 bank, not a qualified registration

partialTraceObservation.detail: Approximate centreline from the ROM-facing bridge end to the upper image boundary along the board-edge corridor. Stops at image boundary; no assigned net, width, native route or via. Overlapping 080404036 and 080401625 photos show neighboring parallel traces; their identity must be tracked without jumping between lanes or confusing opposite-side copper visible through the board.

cpuObservation.detail: Sixth joint from pin 21 on the outer CPU row. No visible underside branch at this joint in the local crop; top-side attachment remains to be traced.

routeReviews.nextEvidence: Follow a continuous path from an individually identified bridge endpoint to A5:26 or V4.9:C, including any layer transition, then check correspondence on the primary specimen. A closed bridge connects both ends, so a continuity beep across it cannot determine terminal order. No bridge opening is requested or implied by this review.

routeReviews.observation: Visible signal-side branch turns toward A1 and enters the gap between its cable-end inner-row leads. The package hides onward attachment. Cable-facing notch confirms the existing primary A1 orientation; the opposite round mould mark is not used to reverse pin order.

comparison.scope: Separate specimen shows a corresponding resistor-to-package-gap path. Supports topology investigation only; no primary coordinates transferred.

rejectedProjection.method: Global top photo board-envelope homography, nominal 0.35 mm width, existing native pads
rejectedProjection.result: Projected candidate intersects A1:13 /A4 while assigned from R10.1:2 /TA_TAKT. Do not interpret this model conflict as measured shorting or change the schematic to fit it.

candidateSegments.detail: Visible top copper toward the A1 package edge. R10.1 signal identity follows the reference schematic. The path disappears beside the package; no A1 pin attachment, under-package continuation, via or cable path is asserted. Nominal planar projection and 0.35 mm width remain estimates.

Estimated native-pad attachment to visible top copper. R10.1 signal identity follows the reference schematic. The path disappears beside the package; no A1 pin attachment, under-package continuation, via or cable path is asserted. Nominal planar projection and 0.35 mm width remain estimates.

drcViolations.description: Front solder mask aperture bridges items with different nets

routeReviews.nextEvidence: Resolve the hidden continuation independently before assigning an A1 endpoint. The local fit does not extend to the outer row; retain the estimated-pad clearance failure.

localRegistration.scope: Board-level inner-row lead-entry observations, independent nearby checks and explicit failed outer-row extrapolation. Only the visible segment inside the local hull is assigned. The rejected global projection is retained; no hidden A1 pin attachment is promoted.

routeReviews.summary: The global top projection was rejected. A bounded local fit supports the visible R10.1 branch beside A1; the under-package attachment remains unresolved.
